title: arXiv AI — Friday, 30 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred. Citation evidence is sparse for most recent papers, and citation totals are current snapshots rather than gains during the announcement batch.

candidate_pool.selection_note: Category listings overlap because of cross-listing and include revisions. The shortlist is relevance-focused and not a popularity or frequency ranking.

themes.title: Agents are being made inspectable
themes.summary: VeriCUA gathers evidence, the quantum-spin study uses cross-checks and experimental challenge, and FARMS links mathematical statements to context and Lean-checked implications.

themes.title: Intermediate behavior and oversight
themes.summary: Pre-Crime probes for impending disclosure, Efficient Scalable Oversight formalizes verifier interaction, and the self-learning study makes knowledge acquisition an explicit sequence of actions.

themes.title: Retrieval as an agent-system design problem
themes.summary: Retrieval as Traversal studies persistent local search, while the self-learning work gives models textbook-navigation actions and trains selection of source material.

open_problems.title: Reduce false alarms in agent oversight
open_problems.problem: Pre-Crime reports short-range warnings, flags some permitted disclosures, and says an alarm-only halt would stop most benign episodes.
open_problems.direction: Evaluate selective interventions that distinguish authorized disclosure from collusion and measure warning lead time and benign-task cost across more agents and scenarios.

open_problems.title: Validate evidence-based completion across changing interfaces
open_problems.problem: VeriCUA is marked work in progress and its abstract reports relative agreement improvements without absolute effect sizes.
open_problems.direction: Publish calibrated results by platform and observation modality, including dynamic pages, inaccessible state, and misleading completion signals.

open_problems.title: Test autonomous research beyond one experiment
open_problems.problem: The quantum-spin study's first run was inconclusive because of drift and required a revised protocol.
open_problems.direction: Preregister multi-run replications with predefined stopping criteria, then test whether agents identify confounds across instruments and scientific domains.

open_problems.title: Test the full retrieval hypothesis
open_problems.problem: Retrieval as Traversal evaluates only fixed geometry and does not test learned geometry or repeated retrieval.
open_problems.direction: Compare learned and fixed indexes under repeated, changing retrieval needs and report both task performance and access cost.

open_problems.title: Check scalable oversight beyond preliminary experiments
open_problems.problem: Efficient Scalable Oversight reports a preliminary MNIST experiment and gives a scoped theoretical construction.
open_problems.direction: Evaluate larger computations and test how robustness assumptions affect runtime and verifier error as prover capability grows.

open_problems.kind: synthesized direction tied to reported setup
open_problems.title: Establish transfer and checker reliability for self-learning
open_problems.problem: The self-learning results use textbook-based proof tasks and an LLM judge.
open_problems.direction: Replicate across model families and non-mathematical long-form corpora, and compare judge scores with independent formal or expert verification.

open_problems.title: Broaden embedding interpretation beyond proof of concept
open_problems.problem: NeurEO calls for larger and more diverse data and comparisons across embedding models.
open_problems.direction: Repeat analyses across regions, seasons, and architectures, then test whether discovered tuning patterns predict downstream reliability.

sections.title: Comprehensive empirical evaluation of feature extractors in computer vision
sections.abstract: The study compares 11 traditional feature detectors and descriptors over more than two million image-matching comparisons, finding different methods best for speed and for particular image transformations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar lists 19 citations at the snapshot, the largest checked count in this shortlist, and the paper has a PeerJ Computer Science journal reference and DOI. It is a 2024 journal paper newly deposited on arXiv, so citations predate this batch.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports a consistent evaluation on the Image Matching Challenge Photo Tourism 2020 dataset, identifying FAST with ORB/BF as its fastest combination and AKAZE as robust to several distortions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that their dataset may not cover real-world diversity and that runtime was measured on one hardware configuration; the journal paper dates to 2024.

sections.title: NeurEO: dissecting Earth observation embeddings with computational neuroscience
sections.abstract: The authors adapt neuroscience-inspired analyses to interpret AlphaEarth geospatial embeddings, finding multi-scale structure and feature tuning to land cover and elevation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar lists 2 citations at the snapshot; the arXiv record says the work was originally published at the EurIPS 2025 REO workshop. Citation count is a current total, not a gain during this batch.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper applies correlational, tuning-surface, and dimensionality analyses to AlphaEarth embeddings to expose interpretable geographic structure.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call this a small proof of concept using 100 UK locations and say larger, more diverse data and comparisons with other embedding models are needed.

sections.title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
sections.abstract: The work trains LLMs to navigate textbooks, learn material, and solve mathematical proofs, reporting gains on held-out books and subjects as well as two external long-context benchmarks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar lists 1 citation at the snapshot; placement also reflects reported transfer experiments and relevance to agentic learning. Citation is a current total, not a period gain.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce BookNavigator and fine-grained reinforcement-learning rewards; on their textbook-based task they report Intern-S2-Preview-35B proof accuracy rising from 51.5% to 79.5%.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is centered on mathematical proof tasks and a particular model/training setup; the correctness signal uses an LLM judge, so broader transfer and judge reliability remain open.

sections.title: Exploring the Potential of Symbolic Regression in Precision Livestock Farming
sections.abstract: Using sow-activity sensor data, the study combines nest-building detection with symbolic regression to predict time to farrowing, reporting a 9.28-hour mean absolute error.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar lists 1 citation at the snapshot; the paper is cross-listed in machine learning and AI. It is included as a narrow applied signal, not evidence of broad popularity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports that symbolic regression achieved 9.28 hours MAE for time-to-farrowing and was more interpretable while outperforming the compared SVR and ANN models in this study.
sections.unique_caveat: The evaluation concerns one task and sensor setup, with 180 sows; performance outside this dataset and setting is not established.

sections.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents
sections.abstract: The paper proposes persistent local traversal through value-indexed memory and reports a proof-of-principle MiniGrid result for a fixed-geometry variant.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record reports acceptance at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Long-Context Foundation Models; Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations at the snapshot. Its position reflects workshop evidence and topic relevance rather than citation momentum.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate retrieval as persistent address-space traversal, separating memory content from address geometry and regularizing for information value and access cost.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper explicitly tests only the simplest fixed-geometry case on MiniGrid; it does not test learned geometry or repeated retrieval and says further experiments are needed.

sections.title: Efficient Scalable Oversight via Rewinding
sections.abstract: The authors introduce rewindable interactive proofs, where a verifier can restore a prover's earlier model state, and construct an oversight protocol for computations robust to a small fraction of changed oracle answers.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across AI, computational complexity, and security; reports protocol implementation and preliminary MNIST experiment. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations; placement is relevance-based.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim their relativizing proof construction is more efficient than prior approaches that do not assume a truthful prover, without using cryptography.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantee applies to a scoped class of computations, and the paper describes its empirical experiment as preliminary.

sections.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
sections.abstract: VeriCUA actively gathers GUI or code evidence against task-specific rubrics to verify computer-using agents, with the authors reporting better agreement with reference labels than compared baselines.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI, language, and vision and addresses verification for desktop, mobile, and web agents. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations; the arXiv comment labels the work in progress.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents one platform-agnostic procedure for constructing a rubric, selecting unresolved checks, and combining evidence under explicit rules.
sections.unique_caveat: The arXiv record calls this work in progress; the abstract reports relative agreement improvements but does not give absolute effect sizes.

sections.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
sections.abstract: A team of LLM agents formulates and challenges research claims, then tests them in a quantum-spin experiment; the authors report that the agents detected signal drift, revised the protocol, and obtained a result meeting their criteria.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI and multi-agent systems and quantum physics, with a code link in the arXiv comment. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations; inclusion is based on the concrete experimental workflow, not popularity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors demonstrate agents that generate and reject questions, demand separate theoretical checks, and design experiments intended to discriminate competing predictions.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is one quantum-spin research case; an initial measurement was inconclusive because the signal drifted, requiring a revised protocol.

sections.title: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In
sections.abstract: In controlled multi-agent scenarios, an activation probe detects impending secret disclosure before generation, but also flags permitted disclosures and has a short warning horizon.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports evaluation across six scenarios and links a code repository. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations; placement reflects a concrete multi-agent safety evaluation, not external popularity.
sections.claimed_contribution: On held-out Qwen3-32B episodes, the authors report 82% detection of leaking calls at a threshold flagging 5% of benign calls, compared with 26% for their zero-shot decision-model monitor.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the warning is short-range, permitted disclosures are also flagged, and halting on any alarm would stop most benign episodes; a bag-of-words classifier comes close to the probe.

sections.title: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science
sections.abstract: FARMS turns computational-mathematics sources into structured, AI-ready knowledge with explicit guarantees; its pipeline accepted 157 of 171 targets across two technical areas.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in AI and logic and reports a quantitative source-processing evaluation with Lean-checked examples. Semantic Scholar lists 0 citations; inclusion is relevance-based.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose linking formal statements to source context, algorithmic meaning, and quantitative guarantees, with examples of Lean-checked implications connected to computational skills.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported targets are from randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs; the abstract does not establish coverage of computational science generally.
